name: IMAGE
description: IMAGE displays an image directly inside a cell by providing a URL to the image file. It can also resize the image and choose how it fits inside the cell.
tldr: IMAGE inserts a picture from a URL into a spreadsheet cell and lets you control its size and cropping.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL of the image to display. Must be a direct link to an image file (e.g., .png, .jpg, .svg).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Sizing mode: 1 = resize to fit, 2 = stretch to fill, 3 = original size, 4 = custom size. Default is 1.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Image height in pixels. Used with mode 4.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Image width in pixels. Used with mode 4.

basicExample.description: Show a logo from a URL inside a cell
basicExample.explanation: The image is fetched from the URL and displayed in the cell, resized to fit.

advancedExamples.title: Custom sized image
advancedExamples.description: Display a product image at a fixed 100x100 pixel size
advancedExamples.explanation: Mode 4 uses the custom height and width arguments.

advancedExamples.title: Image from a dynamic cell URL
advancedExamples.description: Show the image whose URL is stored in another cell
advancedExamples.result: Image stretched to fill the cell
advancedExamples.explanation: Mode 2 stretches the image to fill the cell dimensions. A2 contains the URL.

howItWorks: IMAGE fetches the image from the provided URL and renders it inside the cell. The mode parameter controls how the image is sized: fit, stretch, original size, or custom dimensions. The URL must be publicly accessible and point directly to an image file.

howToSteps.name: Get the image URL
howToSteps.text: Copy the direct link to the image file, not a webpage.

howToSteps.name: Choose a sizing mode
howToSteps.text: Use 1 to fit, 2 to stretch, 3 for original size, or 4 for custom dimensions.

howToSteps.name: Set dimensions if needed
howToSteps.text: For mode 4, add height and width in pixels.

limitations: IMAGE is Google Sheets only. Excel has limited support for images in cells via newer IMAGE function in some versions, but behavior differs.
The URL must be publicly accessible and directly link to an image file.
Images may not print or export to PDF consistently.
Some image hosting sites block direct linking.

commonErrors.cause: The URL is not a direct image link or the site blocks embedding.
commonErrors.fix: Use a direct .jpg/.png URL and test it in a browser.

commonErrors.cause: The mode number is invalid or dimensions are missing for mode 4.
commonErrors.fix: Use 1, 2, 3, or 4. For mode 4, provide both height and width.

commonErrors.cause: Mode 3 displays the image at original size, which may overflow the cell.
commonErrors.fix: Use mode 1 or 4 to resize the image.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: IMAGE is native to Google Sheets. Excel has introduced IMAGE in Microsoft 365 for some users, but availability and behavior differ.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: In Google Sheets, IMAGE works in all versions. In Excel, it depends on the subscription and version.

faq.question: Can I use IMAGE with Google Drive photos?
faq.answer: Only if the image is publicly shared and you have a direct download URL. Standard Google Drive sharing links usually do not work.

faq.question: Can I put an image behind text?
faq.answer: No, IMAGE places the image inside a cell. For floating images, use Insert > Image instead.

faq.question: Does IMAGE work in Excel?
faq.answer: Excel 365 has added IMAGE for some users, but it is not as universally available as in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Can I use SVG images?
faq.answer: Google Sheets supports SVG in IMAGE, but rendering may vary depending on the browser.
